task: The budget-curve unit's mechanism analysis — the sizer chain, the pairing question priced, the amendment's blast radius, the equal-budget arithmetic proven
prompt: UNDERSTAND THE BUDGET-CURVE UNIT'S MECHANISMS — the sizer arm's chain, the equal-budget law, the pairing law, the amendment's blast radius. Read-only analysis; no writes; fail-fast if ground is missing. THE QUESTIONS: (1) THE SIZER'S CHAIN — the binary-threshold model step-by-step: the latent order's positions (1..n), the threshold j in {1..n-1} (the integer midpoints), the true answer deterministic from the truth (position > j), ONE flip draw per judgment at rate p, the round-robin schedule (judgment m uses threshold ((m-1) mod (n-1)) + 1 — walk the arithmetic: at n=10, k=3, B_i=13.5->13/14? THE REMAINDER RULE: r = n/2 items get the ceiling? at n=10, n0=45, k=3: 135 judgments / 10 items = 13.5 — the split: 5 items at 14, 5 at 13 (r=5=n/2) — verify keikaku's claim r = n/2 at every ruled n (n=10: 45*3=135, 135/10=13.5 r=5; n=20: 190*3=570, 570/20=28.5 r=10; n=30: 435*3=1305, 1305/30=43.5 r=15 — YES r=n/2 always: n0*n/2 = n(n-1)/2*n/2... walk it exactly); the per-item score the exact Fraction (yes_count / B_i); the ranking score-descending groups (equal Fractions tied, within-group by id); THE MEASURE'S REUSE — accept_measure consumes (ranked_groups, latent_order): confirm the sizer's groups fit its contract exactly (the flattened ids, the group order); (2) THE PAIRING LAW'S MECHANISM — both arms run from random.Random(seed) fresh instances at the SAME seed: the pairwise arm's first act rng.sample (the latent), the sizer arm's first act THE SAME rng.sample — confirm the latent byte-identical across arms by construction (the same seed, the same first act); the arms' noise draws independent thereafter (each arm's own instance — wait, SAME seed means the noise draws also mirror? NO — read carefully: the pairwise arm's chain (sample then per-judgment draws) and the sizer arm's chain (sample then per-judgment draws) — if both start from random.Random(seed), the FIRST act matches (the latent) but the SUBSEQUENT draws also mirror position-for-position (the same RNG stream!) — is that the intent (the paired-noise form) or should the sizer's instance derive differently (seed + 1? a second sample?)? THE QUESTION FOR THE BRIEF: the noise streams' relationship — identical streams (the strictest pairing, one truth + mirrored noise) vs independent streams (the same truth, independent noise — the more realistic comparison). Price both; the brief rules; (3) THE AMENDMENT'S BLAST RADIUS — accept_run gains quorum: int = ACCEPTANCE_QUORUM: the signature line, the register_run call threading quorum, the default pinned at ACCEPTANCE_QUORUM=3 — the landed suite's behavior byte-identical (the default unchanged); the k=1 point's fresh runs (accept_run(..., quorum=1)); the ONE-line nature verified (what else in acceptance.py references the quorum? the docstring's step-(4) wording); (4) THE EQUAL-BUDGET LAW'S ARITHMETIC — the sizer's total = n0 x quorum exactly (sum B_i = sum of the splits = n0 x quorum — walk the remainder rule's arithmetic at every ruled n x k); the pairwise arm's total (n0 x quorum judgments — each pair judged quorum times); (5) THE RECORD'S DETERMINISM — the sizer record byte-identical across replays (the clock-free surface: the coordinates, the latent, the per-item judgments/scores, the groups, the counts — no stamps anywhere). READ: .plans/ideation/2026-11-21-budget-curve/plan/keikaku-composition.md, src/prioritree/acceptance.py whole, .plans/ideation/2026-11-20-prioritree-core/synthesize/acceptance-brief.md §5, the k=1 baseline table. Operation budget: at most 6 reads. DELIVER (in-message, ~50-70 lines): each chain named step-by-step with the arithmetic walked exactly; the pairing question priced with a recommendation; the amendment's blast radius verified minimal; the equal-budget law proven at every ruled (n, k); the record's determinism surface pinned. No writes — shinko lands it at understand/budget-curve.md.
